subject: Production Throughput Spike & 502s — Odyssey AI impact
messages:
From: Odyssey Support <support@odyssey.ai>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Michael Chen <mchen@odyssey.ai>
Date: 2028-06-05T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Production: elevated 5xx and token throughput drop - Odyssey

Hi team,

We started seeing an uptick in 502/504 responses from the Redwood endpoint serving our chat model at ~09:05 PDT. Concurrently, observed token throughput dropped ~60% and P99 latency spiked from ~120ms to ~2.4s for several request classes.

Attached a small telemetry snapshot and the trace id list. This affects ~12% of live traffic and has begun impacting user experience (sessions are timing out). Can you confirm whether this is a configuration or capacity issue on Redwood's side? We can provide additional logs if useful.

Here are immediate items from our side:
- Local retry backlog increased, customer sessions showing degraded UX
- No deploys on our side around the incident start

Appreciate quick triage and suggested mitigation steps.

--
Eva Laurent
SRE Lead, Odyssey AI
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Odyssey Support <support@odyssey.ai>, Eva Laurent <eva.laurent@odyssey.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-05T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production: elevated 5xx and token throughput drop - Odyssey

Eva — thanks for flagging. We're on it. Short plan:
1) Spinning up an immediate dedicated pool to soak Odyssey baseline traffic (will take ~8-12 min).
2) Triage initial telemetry to identify whether this is scheduling / kernel fallback / network egress.
3) Short-term routing: shift ~30% of Odyssey traffic to the dedicated pool and enable degraded-mode caching to reduce KV lookups.

Marissa / Karthik — can you stand up a bridge (Zoom + PD) and pull the runbook referenced below? I'm attaching the snapshot you sent to the ticket and will post updates in the war-room doc.

Attaching: initial-telemetry-snapshot.png (png)

—David

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Date: 2028-06-05T10:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production: elevated 5xx and token throughput drop - Odyssey — Initial triage

On Mon, Jun 5, 2028 at 9:15 AM Odyssey Support <support@odyssey.ai> wrote:
> We started seeing an uptick in 502/504 responses from the Redwood endpoint serving our chat model at ~09:05 PDT. Concurrently, observed token throughput dropped ~60% and P99 latency spiked from ~120ms to ~2.4s for several request classes.
>
> Attached a small telemetry snapshot and the trace id list.

Status update from infra/serving:
- Observed a sudden shift to fallback single-threaded kernels for a portion of the serving fleet — correlates with the time window reported. Suspect a late-stage quantized kernel selector regression triggered by a new sequence-length distribution in production traffic.
- No infra rebalances detected in us-west-2 that would account for capacity loss.
- Action taken: forced a compatible kernel override on the impacted node pool and increased per-instance concurrency cap to reduce queueing.

Attachments: heap-trace.log (partial) — contains the stack traces from a sample process showing the kernel selection path and retries.

Next steps:
1) Continue to flush KV/prefix cache and monitor p99.
2) Keep dedicated pool live for Odyssey until we validate stability for 12h.
3) Prepare a rollback of the kernel selector change (if upstream diff is identified) for a canary rollback tonight.

Karthik
Staff Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Eva Laurent <eva.laurent@odyssey.ai>, Michael Chen <mchen@odyssey.ai>, Odyssey Support <support@odyssey.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-05T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production: elevated 5xx and token throughput drop - Odyssey — Status update

Eva / Michael — quick update from the war-room: 
- Root cause (working hypothesis): regression in kernel selector triggered by an unexpected shift in sequence length distribution from a subset of Odyssey traffic. This caused fallback to higher-latency kernels and increased queueing leading to 502s.
- Mitigations applied: forced kernel override on affected pool, increased per-instance concurrency cap, enabled degraded-mode prefix caching, and spun up a dedicated pool for Odyssey traffic.
- Observed impact: token throughput recovered to ~92% of baseline within 18 minutes of mitigations; 5xx rate reduced to ~0.3% (initially peaked at ~3.8%).
- ETA for full validation: 12 hours of stable telemetry; our team will watch P50/P95/P99 and error rates.

We will keep the dedicated pool live and keep you posted on the 30/60/120 minute marks. Attaching the runbook we used.

If you need immediate rollback to previous kernel selector behavior on your traffic, we can schedule a canary; let us know.

Regards,
David Kim
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Eva Laurent <eva.laurent@odyssey.ai>, Michael Chen <mchen@odyssey.ai>, Odyssey Support <support@odyssey.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-06T17:03:00-07:00
Subject: Incident wrap & next steps — Odyssey throughput spike (PD-9921)

Afternoon all — final update for PD-9921. 

Summary: the dedicated pool remained healthy through the validation window. P99 latency returned to nominal (~140ms) and error rate stabilized below our SLO threshold (0.2%) after the kernel override + concurrency adjustments. We completed a partial canary rollback overnight to validate the selector code path; that rollback confirmed the regression is triggered only by a narrow sequence-length pattern we discussed.

Customer impact: estimated 12% of sessions experienced degraded UX during the 09:05–09:40 window on 6/5. No data loss or request misrouting detected.

Action items:
- Engineering (Karthik): implement a hard guard in kernel selector for the specific sequence-length bucket and ship a patch (ETA: 48 hours).
- Infra (Grace): add an automated early-detection alert for sudden kernel-fallback rates (ETA: 7 days).
- CS/Account (Marissa/Ben): propose a customer credit gesture; draft sent to Legal and Finance for approval (Marissa to follow up).
- Customer comms: Ben to send a concise post-mortem and timeline to Odyssey by EOD tomorrow.

Attachments: redwood-ld-runbook-v2.pdf, heap-trace.log (trimmed)

Thanks everyone for the rapid mobilization. I'll file the incident post-mortem and link the final notes in HS-98234.

—David
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
